Prepared remarks about the quarter.

Question-and-Answer Session

Operator: Your first question comes from the line of Brian Nowak with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.
Brian Nowak: Thanks for taking my questions. I have 2, 1 on Muse, 1 on Enterprise. What are the constraints to the slope of forward user growth? And the second 1 is on enterprise. Mark, can you walk us through your vision for the Meta Enterprise product offering?
Mark Elliot Zuckerberg -- Chief Executive Officer: We have more than 10 million people in the US and Canada who have set it up. One of the biggest constraints is that this is a compute intensive service to run, so we have not launched it globally yet. The pro is that you have 10 million people using it in the first 6 weeks. The compute efficiency work is going to be important because we want enough compute to serve a billion plus people. Doing that in tandem with bringing down the compute cost is going to be important. Muse launched first on Muse Spark, the default across the free tier. Muse Wonder is in the paid tier.
Transitioning to talking about the enterprise piece, the main enterprise offering in the near term is the model API and Muse code, and business agents for sales and customer support. Each of those 3 things is growing quite quickly. Over time we want a business network of Muse agents that can work with each other.
Susan J. Li -- Chief Financial Officer: I would add on to Mark's comments on enterprise. We do not believe that traditional enterprise companies have this lockdown. Already today, we have 500 million businesses using our products. This can support subscriptions and usage based API and messaging. We intend to scale our investment behind demonstrated customer demand and product market fit.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Eric Sheridan with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.
Eric Sheridan: How do you think about friction around agentic commerce when suppliers do not want agents on their platforms?
Mark Elliot Zuckerberg -- Chief Executive Officer: Overwhelmingly, businesses are very excited about enabling this.
Susan J. Li -- Chief Financial Officer: I think agents are going to be an important part of how reality evolves, and the market will move towards permissioned structured interactions.
